transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

I guess what brought me in is I’ve been kind of… ramped up. I’m usually just a regular crew guy at work, but I started trying to handle three bids at once, calling city people, lining up plant suppliers, and messaging everybody I know about this park idea. It felt like I couldn’t shut it off.
Have you had episodes like this before, where you felt unusually energized or couldn’t slow down?

Yeah. I mean, I’ve had times like that. I’d be up before daylight loading tools, sketching out planting beds, pricing native plants… then after working outside all day, I still felt like I needed to keep going. Like stopping just didn’t feel right.
Have there been times when your mood was noticeably different—like unusually high, excited, or even irritable—along with this increased energy?

Yeah. Before I crashed, I felt really fired up… like bigger than myself, kind of. And if someone at work questioned my plan or told me I needed to slow down, I’d snap at them way harder than it called for. Like it didn’t take much to set me off.
Have you ever had a period where your mood was really elevated or irritable most of the day, nearly every day, for several days in a row?

Yeah, I think so. For several days I felt really fired up, like I was bigger than myself almost. But it wasn’t all good energy — if a coworker questioned what I was doing or told me to slow down, I’d snap at him way harder than made sense.
Can you tell me how many days in a row you felt this way before it started to get better or you 'crashed'?
It was about two weeks, I’d say. It started when I got really wrapped up in remaking myself for that park pitch, and I stayed fired up and overconfident like that until I finally crashed.
After you 'crashed' from that two-week period, did you feel unusually down, depressed, or lose interest in things you normally enjoy?

Yeah. After that, I just kind of stopped caring about stuff I usually like. I used to go hiking to clear my head and take pictures of creek beds or trees, but lately I’ll leave the camera in the truck. Even if the light’s perfect, I just… don’t really care.
After you crashed, did you feel down or lose interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?
Yes. It’s been more than two weeks — honestly, it’s been hanging over me for about a year now. And after this last crash, it’s the worst it’s gotten.
